title: Why Mirrors Won
question: Why did big research telescopes end up using mirrors?
hook: Lenses came first, yet almost every giant telescope today is built around a mirror.
idea: A lens telescope cannot grow past about 1 meter, so large research telescopes are reflectors.

beats.prompt: Astronomers around 1900 want the largest possible light-gathering element for a research telescope. What do they choose?

choices.label: A bigger and bigger glass lens
choices.feedback: It tempts because lenses came first, but lens telescopes stop at about 1 meter.

choices.label: A radio dish
choices.feedback: A dish collects radio waves, which is a different job from large visible-light research telescopes.

beats.explain: Refracting telescopes top out at about 1 meter, so the vast majority of large optical research telescopes built since 1900 are reflectors.

beats.prompt: Put these telescope events in order.
items: Hans Lipperhey submits a patent for a refracting telescope
Isaac Newton builds the first practical reflecting telescope
beats.explain: The patent came in 1608, Galileo built his in 1609, Newton built his reflector in 1668, and the achromatic lens arrived in 1733.

beats.prompt: Match each space telescope to what it is known for.
beats.explain: Each is a space telescope, and each is known for a different job or orbit.

beats.prompt: Sort each kind of light by where it can be observed.
beats.explain: The atmosphere is opaque to most of the spectrum, so only visible, near-infrared and some radio waves reach the ground.
